extracted.intended_audience: general public, policymakers, and public health professionals
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the U.S. opioid epidemic covering epidemiology, demographic disparities, legal actions, federal/state countermeasures, and recommended/implemented public-health interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS 'Opioid Strategy' five aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Health and Human Services announced their 'Opioid Strategy' consisting of five aims: (1) Improve access to prevention, treatment, and recovery support services; (2) Target the availability and distribution of overdose-reversing drugs to ensure broad provision, focusing on high-risk populations; (3) Strengthen public health data reporting and collection to improve timeliness and specificity and inform a real-time public health response; (4) Support cutting-edge research that advances understanding of pain and addiction and identifies effective public health interventions; (5) Advance the practice of pain management to enable access to high-quality, evidence-based pain care while reducing inappropriate opioid use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five aims frame federal priorities for reducing opioid-related health harms, from prevention and treatment access to data improvements, research, and pain-management practice change.

rubrics_metrics.name: State law categories to stifle high-risk prescribing
rubrics_metrics.description: New state laws fell primarily into one of the following four categories: Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) enrollment laws; PDMP query laws; Opioid prescribing cap laws; Pill mill laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists these four categories as the main legislative approaches states used to reduce high-risk opioid prescribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDMP enrollment laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribers must enroll in their state's PDMP, an electronic database containing a record of all patients' controlled substance prescriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment is a prerequisite to using the monitoring system; intended to ensure providers are registered to report and access prescription histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDMP query laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribers must check the PDMP before prescribing an opioid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring prescribers to consult the PDMP is intended to detect possible doctor-shopping or dangerous polypharmacy prior to issuing an opioid prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opioid prescribing cap laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Opioid prescriptions cannot exceed designated doses or durations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps are a statutory limit on initial or total prescribed opioid dose/duration to reduce risk of long-term use and diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pill mill laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Pain clinics are closely regulated and monitored to minimize the prescription of opioids non-medically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These laws target clinics that inappropriately dispense or prescribe opioids to curb non-medical prescribing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure and Responsible Drug Disposal Act (2010) amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controlled Substances Act was amended to allow pharmacies to accept controlled substances from households or long-term care facilities in their drug disposal programs or 'take-back' programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural change facilitates safe disposal of unused medications to reduce diversion and accidental ingestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA requirement for manufacturer-sponsored prescriber education
rubrics_metrics.description: The US Food and Drug Administration required manufacturers of long-acting opioids to sponsor educational programs for prescribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulatory approach aims to change prescribing behavior via industry-sponsored training; the page notes it is unclear whether these programs have a positive effect on reducing opioid prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for pharmacists, nurses, and physicians on appropriate opioid prescribing
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first time, pharmacists, nurses, and physicians would have training made available on appropriate prescribing of opioid medicines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional training is presented as a component of regulatory/federal response to improve safe prescribing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act (CARA, 2016)
rubrics_metrics.description: CARA expands opioid addiction treatment with buprenorphine and authorizes millions of dollars in funding for opioid research and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CARA is cited as a federal legislative measure to increase treatment capacity and fund research/intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21st Century Cures Act funding for states
rubrics_metrics.description: The 21st Century Cures Act includes $1 billion in state grants to fight the opioid epidemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a large federal funding stream for state-level prevention, treatment, and recovery programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Act (H.R. 6) provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The SUPPORT Act includes Medicare and Medicaid reform to improve treatment, recovery, and prevention efforts while also strengthening the fight against synthetic drugs like fentanyl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute bundles multiple provisions (including elements from other acts) intended to expand access to care and control synthetic opioid threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of PDMPs with health information technology and centralized data-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal and state interventions are working on employing health information technology in order to expand the impact of existing drug monitoring programs; research shows promising results when a state integrates drug monitoring programs with health information technologies and shares data through a centralized platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best-practice implementation detail: technical integration and centralized sharing can improve timeliness and usefulness of prescription-monitoring data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeled combined-intervention impact (reduce prescribing + naloxone + expand treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision-analytical model found that, compared to status quo projections, a combination of reducing opioid prescribing, increasing naloxone distribution, and expanding treatment for opioid use disorder was associated with a large number of lives saved (model figure: an estimated 179,151 lives saved vs 484,429 projected deaths under status quo between 2020–2029).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites modeling evidence supporting multi-pronged interventions (prevention, harm reduction, and treatment expansion) as an effective policy mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law enforcement and trade restrictions on fentanyl shipments
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive actions ordering U.S. carriers to search for and refuse deliveries of fentanyl from abroad and other measures to block shipments of fentanyl coming from other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply-control measures via mail/carrier enforcement and international trade restrictions are presented as part of the federal response to synthetic opioids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal accountability through criminal prosecution and civil litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecutions (e.g., Insys Therapeutics executives convicted for bribery and fraud) and large-scale civil litigation and settlements against manufacturers and distributors (multibillion-dollar settlements and county/state lawsuits alleging public nuisance) are used to hold industry actors accountable and recover funds for prevention/treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents both criminal and civil legal strategies as policy tools to deter misconduct and finance remedial programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal grant programs and targeted funding (e.g., Opioid State Targeted Response grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration administers Opioid State Targeted Response grants (two-year program authorized by the 21st Century Cures Act) which provided $485 million to states and US territories in fiscal year 2017 for preventing and combating opioid misuse and addiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted grants are a mechanism to distribute federal dollars to state/territorial efforts for prevention, treatment, and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls to suspend new opioid approvals due to oversight concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: In March 2019, two FDA specialists publicly demanded that the FDA suspend new opioid approvals, alleging that the FDA's oversight of opioid approvals had been dangerously deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represents a regulatory-evaluation stance arguing for stricter approval controls to limit new opioid products entering the market.
